Classical / PQC style: classical-style

≈HEURISTIC

hal_crypto/identify/classical-vs-pqc

evidence-based guess, never a proof

confidence: 0.85

The structures found (lfsr-stream) are the ones classical symmetric primitives are built from, and no lattice/ring arithmetic was found. This does NOT rule out post-quantum cryptography: a hash-based or code-based scheme contains neither NTTs nor S-boxes and would come back none-detected here.

structural crypto pattern match (kind: structural, unbounded)

A 93-stage NLFSR: the feedback has degree 2 and is coupled to chain(s) 1

✔PROVEN

hal_crypto/nlfsr/feedback/0

holds for every execution, given the listed assumptions

unbounded claimthe feedback cone was enumerated exhaustively

The chain is closed by a feedback function that is not linear, so it has no feedback polynomial. Its algebraic normal form is s0[68] ^ s1[110] ^ s1[65] ^ (s1[108] & s1[109]). 4 of its inputs are stages of chain(s) 1 rather than of this one, so the register is closed through a sibling: a Trivium/Grain-style coupled generator, whose state is the union of the coupled chains. The shift links are only visible with start held at 0: every stage's next state is a multiplexer, which is what a parallel load looks like after synthesis. The claim is therefore about the netlist in that operating mode.

Method

exhaustive cone evaluation (kind: simulation, unbounded)

Enumerates the whole input space of a combinational cone using only the tennm_lcell_comb semantics in hal_agilex.primitives, and reads the truth table off it. Exhaustive, so the resulting table is the function, not a sample of it.

Assumptions

idkindassumptionchecked?
primitive-semanticslibrarytennm_lcell_comb and tennm_ff behave as documented in hal_agilex.primitives, which was validated by simulating real Quartus exports against the RTL they were synthesised from.not stated
reader-completenesstoolThe .vo reader refuses Verilog it does not understand, so no instance can have been dropped silently before the analysis ran.checked by this run

A 111-stage NLFSR: the feedback has degree 2 and is coupled to chain(s) 2

✔PROVEN

hal_crypto/nlfsr/feedback/1

holds for every execution, given the listed assumptions

unbounded claimthe feedback cone was enumerated exhaustively

The chain is closed by a feedback function that is not linear, so it has no feedback polynomial. Its algebraic normal form is s1[86] ^ s2[68] ^ s2[83] ^ (s2[81] & s2[82]). 4 of its inputs are stages of chain(s) 2 rather than of this one, so the register is closed through a sibling: a Trivium/Grain-style coupled generator, whose state is the union of the coupled chains. The shift links are only visible with start held at 0: every stage's next state is a multiplexer, which is what a parallel load looks like after synthesis. The claim is therefore about the netlist in that operating mode.

Method

exhaustive cone evaluation (kind: simulation, unbounded)

Enumerates the whole input space of a combinational cone using only the tennm_lcell_comb semantics in hal_agilex.primitives, and reads the truth table off it. Exhaustive, so the resulting table is the function, not a sample of it.

Assumptions

idkindassumptionchecked?
primitive-semanticslibrarytennm_lcell_comb and tennm_ff behave as documented in hal_agilex.primitives, which was validated by simulating real Quartus exports against the RTL they were synthesised from.not stated
reader-completenesstoolThe .vo reader refuses Verilog it does not understand, so no instance can have been dropped silently before the analysis ran.checked by this run
